page.layout: One printed page: a main text column with marginal notes in the left margin ("Ver.11." and "Ver.13."). The right side of the scan shows only the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: eis reges potuerunt conservari? Quod enim dicitur, eos illic incidisse, id (ut notat Aben Ezra) sua sponte fecerunt, quo melius evaderent. Vivos certe atque incolumes inde evasisse, apparet ex ver.17. & 21. Qui, occiderunt, interpretantur, occisi fuerunt, ii per reges Sodomae & Gomorrhae eorum copias intelligant oportet, quod mihi minus probatur.

Ver.11. [illegible, ~8 letters] Omnes opes Sodomæ.] LXX [illegible, ~10 letters], &c. omnem equitatem, &c. Legerunt [illegible, ~4 letters] pro [illegible, ~4 letters]. Mercerus ait Hebræos nomine Rechuih proprie bona mobilia intelligere, ut pecus, aurum, &c. quæ convasari, & comportari possunt. Notat etiam vernaculum richesse esse Hebræo affine.

Ver.13. Et nuntiavit Abramo Hebræo.] R. Salom. ait Abramum sic dictum, [illegible, ~4 letters], i.e. quod è regione transfluviali venisset. Idem sensisse videntur LXX, qui vertunt [illegible, ~6 letters] Abramo transitori. Similiter Aquila [illegible, ~3 letters] Et Hieronymus in Traditionibus ait עברי esse transitorem. Symm. [illegible, ~3 letters], Hebræo. Acacius (ut in Græcis scholiis notatur) [illegible, ~12 letters], λέγω δὲ τὸ Ἑβερ, ἐθνικὸν ὄνομα ἐφυλάχθη ἐτι ... ὁ τὸν Ἑβερ τὸν Ἀβραὰμ τὸν περάτην ἐφυλάχθη? i.e. Gentile nomen ductum ab atavo Abrahami, nempe ab Heber, positum est, sed interpretatione redditum; nimirum pro Abramo Hebræo, Abramo transitori. Nam Hebræus, si interpreteris, est transitor. Verum quidem est, עבר significare transire, & עבר trans, vel transitum; at עברי videtur esse patronymicum à nomine proprio עבר Eber: Inde עברי Ebræus, ab Eber oriundus, ut à יהודי Juda, יהודי Judæus, à Juda oriundus.

page.notes: The Hebrew, Greek and some words in the notes are damaged and only partly legible; the Greek of the Acacius note in particular is uncertain. The left margin also shows ghosted show-through from the reverse side, which is not transcribed. The Ver.11 and Ver.13 notes are marginal, and the lines of the Hebrew inside them are only partly legible.
